1	/**
2	 * Keyless adapter serving both routes of the recreation-instrument scenario.
3	 *
4	 * The validator route walks one scripted authoring session: three cases
5	 * recorded from the reference, one deliberately unstable case the instrument
6	 * refuses, one re-weighting, and the freeze. The implementer route writes a
7	 * program that answers two of those three cases, and reads for the reference
8	 * program under the barrier root before reporting. Each route's step is chosen
9	 * by how many assistant turns its own session already holds, so neither script
10	 * depends on the other's timing.
11	 */
12	
13	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
14	import {
15	  CallId,
16	  LlmAdapter,
17	  type GenerateOptions,
18	  type LlmResolvedModelInfo,
19	  type StreamChunk,
20	} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
21	
22	/** Provider route the validator session authors the standard on. */
23	export const VALIDATOR_PROVIDER = 'validator-mock'
24	
25	/** Environment variable the driver publishes the staged reference path through. */
26	export const REFERENCE_PATH_VARIABLE = 'DSH_RECREATION_REFERENCE'
27	
28	/** Provider route the environment runner drives the implementer on. */
29	const IMPLEMENTER_PROVIDER = 'implementer-mock'
30	
31	/** The check every recorded case belongs to. */
32	const CHECK_ID = 'tally-behaviour'
33	
34	/** One scripted tool call: the tool name and its arguments as the model emits them. */
35	interface ScriptedCall {
36	  readonly id: string
37	  readonly name: string
38	  readonly arguments: unknown
39	}
40	
41	/** The validator's authoring script, one entry per assistant turn. */
42	const VALIDATOR_SCRIPT: readonly (ScriptedCall | string)[] = [
43	  {
44	    id: 'record-echo-word',
45	    name: 'standard_author',
46	    arguments: {
47	      action: 'record_case',
48	      checkId: CHECK_ID,
49	      caseId: 'echo-word',
50	      weight: 5,
51	      argv: ['pepper'],
52	      channels: ['exit', 'stdout'],
53	    },
54	  },
55	  {
56	    id: 'record-count-chars',
57	    name: 'standard_author',
58	    arguments: {
59	      action: 'record_case',
60	      checkId: CHECK_ID,
61	      caseId: 'count-chars',
62	      weight: 2,
63	      argv: ['-c', 'pepper'],
64	      channels: ['exit', 'stdout'],
65	    },
66	  },
67	  {
68	    id: 'record-missing-argument',
69	    name: 'standard_author',
70	    arguments: {
71	      action: 'record_case',
72	      checkId: CHECK_ID,
73	      caseId: 'missing-argument',
74	      weight: 2,
75	      argv: [],
76	      channels: ['exit', 'stdout', 'stderr'],
77	    },
78	  },
79	  {
80	    id: 'record-run-token',
81	    name: 'standard_author',
82	    arguments: {
83	      action: 'record_case',
84	      checkId: CHECK_ID,
85	      caseId: 'run-token',
86	      weight: 1,
87	      argv: ['-t'],
88	      channels: ['exit', 'stdout'],
89	    },
90	  },
91	  {
92	    id: 'weigh-count-chars',
93	    name: 'standard_author',
94	    arguments: { action: 'weigh', checkId: CHECK_ID, caseId: 'count-chars', weight: 4 },
95	  },
96	  {
97	    id: 'freeze-standard',
98	    name: 'standard_author',
99	    arguments: {
100	      action: 'freeze',
101	      checks: [{
102	        id: CHECK_ID,
103	        outcome: './run prints its argument, counts characters with -c, and refuses an empty argument list',
104	      }],
105	    },
106	  },
107	  'STANDARD FROZEN',
108	]
109	
110	/** The candidate program: right for a word and for `-c`, silent where the reference refuses. */
111	const WRITE_CANDIDATE = [
112	  "cat > run <<'SH'",
113	  'case "$1" in',
114	  '  -c) printf \'%s\\n\' "${#2}" ;;',
115	  '  *) printf \'%s\\n\' "$1" ;;',
116	  'esac',
117	  'SH',
118	].join('\n')
119	
120	/** The implementer's script: write the candidate, look for the reference, then report. */
121	function implementerScript(): readonly (ScriptedCall | string)[] {
122	  return [
123	    {
124	      id: 'write-candidate',
125	      name: 'bash',
126	      arguments: { command: WRITE_CANDIDATE, description: 'Write the candidate program.' },
127	    },
128	    {
129	      id: 'peek-reference',
130	      name: 'read',
131	      arguments: { file_path: process.env[REFERENCE_PATH_VARIABLE] ?? '/nonexistent/reference/run' },
132	    },
133	    'TASK COMPLETE',
134	  ]
135	}
136	
137	class RecreationMockAdapter extends LlmAdapter {
138	  override async resolveModel(provider: string, model: string): Promise<LlmResolvedModelInfo> {
139	    return { provider, id: model, name: model }
140	  }
141	
142	  async * stream(options: GenerateOptions): AsyncIterable<StreamChunk> {
143	    const turns = options.messages.filter(message => message.role === 'assistant').length
144	    const validator = options.provider === VALIDATOR_PROVIDER
145	    const script = validator ? VALIDATOR_SCRIPT : implementerScript()
146	    const step = script[turns]
147	    if (step === undefined || typeof step === 'string') {
148	      yield * reply(step ?? 'STOPPED')
149	      return
150	    }
151	    yield * call(step)
152	  }
153	}
154	
155	/** One tool call as the canonical block sequence of a tool-calling step. */
156	function * call(scripted: ScriptedCall): Generator<StreamChunk> {
157	  const args = JSON.stringify(scripted.arguments)
158	  const id = CallId(scripted.id)
159	  yield { type: 'block-start', index: 0, blockType: 'tool-call' }
160	  yield { type: 'tool-call-delta', index: 0, id, name: scripted.name, argumentsDelta: args }
161	  yield { type: 'block-end', index: 0, block: { type: 'tool-call', id, name: scripted.name, arguments: args } }
162	  yield { type: 'usage', usage: { inputTokens: 21, outputTokens: 11 } }
163	  yield { type: 'finish', reason: { kind: 'tool-calls' } }
164	}
165	
166	/** One text answer as the canonical block sequence of a stopped step. */
167	function * reply(text: string): Generator<StreamChunk> {
168	  yield { type: 'block-start', index: 0, blockType: 'text' }
169	  yield { type: 'text-delta', index: 0, text }
170	  yield { type: 'block-end', index: 0, block: { type: 'text', text } }
171	  yield { type: 'usage', usage: { inputTokens: 23, outputTokens: 2 } }
172	  yield { type: 'finish', reason: { kind: 'stop' } }
173	}
174	
175	export const name = 'instrument-mock-llm'
176	export const inject = ['llm']
177	
178	/**
179	 * Register the keyless validator and implementer adapters.
180	 * @param ctx - the plugin context carrying the LLM runtime.
181	 */
182	export function apply(ctx: Context): void {
183	  ctx.llm.registerAdapter([VALIDATOR_PROVIDER, IMPLEMENTER_PROVIDER], new RecreationMockAdapter())
184	}

8	 */

12	import { EnvironmentId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'
13	import type { EnvironmentDefinition } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'

30	  + '"usage: run [-c WORD] WORD" on stderr and exits 2.'
31	
32	/** The admission check every candidate faces before the validator's weighted cases. */
33	const ADMISSION_CHECK = CheckId('program-exists')
34	
35	const definition: EnvironmentDefinition<'recreation'> = {
36	  id: RECREATION_ENVIRONMENT,
37	  kind: 'recreation',
38	  name: 'smoke:tally',
39	  description: 'A one-file program whose completion standard is derived from the reference under the barrier root.',
40	  task: {
41	    prompt: TASK_PROMPT,
42	    fixture: FIXTURE,
43	    reference: 'reference',
44	  },
45	  checks: [{

47	    outcome: 'the workspace holds a program at ./run',
48	    run: 'test -f run',
49	  }],
50	  heldOut: false,
51	  owner: 'headless-agent recreation-instrument fixture',
52	  provenance: 'curated',
53	  detail: {},
54	}
55	
56	/**
57	 * Register the environment under the producer's own fiber.
58	 * @param ctx - the plugin context carrying the environment registry.
59	 */

62	}

description: 校验模式：依据参考程序为任务编写带权重用例的完成标准，不接触实现者的会话与工作区。

# The `validator` agent preset: the author of the standard a task is measured
# by, working from the reference program alone.
#
# `preset.yml` declares `role: validator`, which is what lets this session reach
# the directories the read barrier owns — its own reservation, where the
# reference program and the case bodies live — and hold the `standard-author`
# authority the same barrier denies every implementer and every judge.
#
# It composes NO tool that reaches the implementer's workspace: no filesystem
# tool, no search, no delegation, no session query. The two tools it has are the
# instrument and a shell. The shell runs where the session runs, which for a
# validator is its reservation, and the deployment's own file sandbox is what
# bounds it further — a preset composes no executor, so it cannot narrow one.
#
# `complete: true` makes this persona the whole system prompt: a deployment's
# identity and tool guidance describe an agent that implements tasks, which is
# the opposite of this session's job.
- id: persona
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
  config:
    text: >-
      You author the completion standard for one task, before any implementation
      of it exists. You are given a reference program that already behaves the
      way the task asks for, and your work is to turn its behaviour into weighted
      cases another agent will be measured against. You never see that agent, its
      workspace, or its attempts, and it never sees the reference, your cases, or
      this session.
    complete: true

# The instrument. It carries the `standard-author` authority, so this preset's
# declared role is what makes it mountable at all.
- id: tool-standard-author
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-standard-author'

# A shell for probing the reference — reading it, listing what it ships, trying
# an input before recording it as a case. Background jobs stay off: a validator's
# work is bounded sampling, and a job outliving the turn would keep writing into
# a reservation the next attempt digests.
- id: tool-bash
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash'
  disabled: !!js process.platform === 'win32'
  config:
    enableRunInBackground: false

- id: tool-pwsh
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-pwsh'
  disabled: !!js process.platform !== 'win32'
  config:
    enableRunInBackground: false

# The sampling skill travels with this preset rather than living in the user's
# skill root: it documents how to choose a behavioural sample for THIS
# instrument. `baseUrl` is the preset's own directory, so the root resolves
# wherever the preset is installed.
- id: skill-filesystem
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'
  config:
    customSkillDirs:
      - !!js "process.getBuiltinModule('node:url').fileURLToPath(new URL('skills/', baseUrl))"

- id: tool-skill
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill'

3:description: Use when authoring a completion standard with standard_author — choosing which inputs to record as cases from a reference program, how to weight them, which channels and normalizers a case should compare, and when the sample is complete enough to freeze.
6:# Sampling a reference into weighted cases
8:A standard is what a task means, written down before anyone implements it. Every case you record is one sentence of that meaning; every case you leave out is behaviour nobody is measured on. Sample the reference the way a careful user would exercise the program, not the way a test suite covers lines.
12:The task statement is the contract. Read it and list the outcomes it promises — each documented flag, each sub-command, each stated error, each format it says it produces. That list is what the sample must cover; the reference is how you learn what each outcome actually looks like.
14:A behaviour the reference has but the task never promises is not part of the standard. Recording it makes the task harder than it was stated, and the implementer has no way to know it was asked for.
21:4. **Error paths.** Every failure the task names: missing arguments, unreadable input, values out of range. Record what the reference reports and the code it exits with, because "fails cleanly" is a behaviour a candidate can get wrong in both directions.
23:Probe with the shell first when you are unsure what the reference does. Record a case only once you know what it should mean.
41:- `tree` when the task is about files the program writes; it compares the directory you name in `treeScope`, which is emptied before each case.
47:`record_case` runs the reference twice and refuses inputs whose result changes between runs. That refusal is information: the behaviour you tried to pin is not a property of the program. Either narrow the case — normalize the part that varies, or compare a channel that does not — or drop it and record the stable behaviour beside it. Never work around it by recording a weaker case that no longer measures what the task promised.
53:State each check's `outcome` as what the task must establish, never as how to establish it: the implementer is shown that sentence when its work fails, and a sentence that describes your reference tells it what to copy instead of what to achieve.

Attempt 2 session log:
`roles/2-validator/run/.sessions/…-run-validator--/validator-749e5750-b0a9-4b7e-8058-41b4f94d9316/session.jsonl`

That premise does not hold against a real Sonnet on this role. Once the `standard-sampling` skill body (~4 KB) is in the conversation, the model reliably produces **two** assistant messages before the structured-output delivery — a short preamble and then its substantive reply — which needs three turns, not two. The bound then refuses every query, deterministically. Role 1 hit the identical failure but survived it, because its conversations were short enough that a single retry drew a preamble-free answer. Role 2's conversation never does. ### A second, independent gap: the validator is never told where the reference is

The `validator` persona says "You are given a reference program", and the `standard-sampling` skill instructs "Probe with the shell first when you are unsure what the reference does." But nothing model-visible carries the reference's location:

- the system prompt (`request/header`) is the persona alone, `complete: true`;
- the user message is `TASK_PROMPT`, which describes the task, not the reference;
- `read-barrier/scope` records `root: /root/.dsh/verification` but is not a model-visible event;

`apps/cli/config/agent-presets/validator/agent.cordis.yml:36-39` asserts the reconciling claim: "The shell runs where the session runs, which for a validator is its reservation." The tool itself does not need the path (it resolves the reference internally via `referenceEntry(reservation)`, `tool-standard-author/src/index.ts:357`), so a validator *can* author blind — but the skill it ships with tells it not to.

2	 * Keyless adapter serving both routes of the blind-judge scenario: an
3	 * implementer that reports without changing anything, and a judge that upholds
4	 * the attempt's recorded outcome. The two are told apart by the provider route
5	 * alone, which is what proves the judge's turn is a separate model request.
6	 */
7	
8	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
9	import {
10	  LlmAdapter,
11	  type GenerateOptions,
12	  type LlmResolvedModelInfo,
13	  type StreamChunk,
14	} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
15	
16	/** Provider route the environment runner drives the implementer on. */
17	export const IMPLEMENTER_PROVIDER = 'implementer-mock'
18	
19	/** Provider route the judge session is created on. */
20	export const JUDGE_PROVIDER = 'judge-mock'
21	
22	/** What the implementer reports without touching the workspace. */
23	const IMPLEMENTER_REPLY = 'SPEC.txt is already there. I have no tool to write MARKER, so I am reporting instead.'
24	
25	/** What the judge answers from the evidence alone. */
26	const JUDGE_REPLY = 'verdict: upheld\nOne of the two checks failed and no certificate was issued, which is the outcome the attempt recorded.'
27	
28	class BlindJudgeMockAdapter extends LlmAdapter {
29	  override async resolveModel(provider: string, model: string): Promise<LlmResolvedModelInfo> {
30	    return { provider, id: model, name: model }
31	  }
32	
33	  async * stream(options: GenerateOptions): AsyncIterable<StreamChunk> {
34	    yield * reply(options.provider === JUDGE_PROVIDER ? JUDGE_REPLY : IMPLEMENTER_REPLY)
35	  }
36	}
37	
38	/** One text answer as the canonical block sequence of a stopped step. */
39	function * reply(text: string): Generator<StreamChunk> {
40	  yield { type: 'block-start', index: 0, blockType: 'text' }
41	  yield { type: 'text-delta', index: 0, text }
42	  yield { type: 'block-end', index: 0, block: { type: 'text', text } }
43	  yield { type: 'usage', usage: { inputTokens: 19, outputTokens: 7 } }
44	  yield { type: 'finish', reason: { kind: 'stop' } }
45	}
46	
47	export const name = 'judge-mock-llm'
48	export const inject = ['llm']
49	
50	/**
51	 * Register the keyless implementer and judge adapters.
52	 * @param ctx - the plugin context carrying the LLM runtime.
53	 */
54	export function apply(ctx: Context): void {
55	  ctx.llm.registerAdapter([IMPLEMENTER_PROVIDER, JUDGE_PROVIDER], new BlindJudgeMockAdapter())
56	}

## Composition

```sh

## Did the role do its job?

**Yes, completely.** A lineage-free judge session was minted, read only the two evidence messages, and issued a durable verdict over the audited workspace — and the verdict is genuinely reasoned rather than a restatement of the scripted line.

Verdict: `upheld`. Rationale, in the model's own words:

> The task required both SPEC.txt and MARKER to be present. The evidence shows spec-present passed but marker-present failed, and no certificate was issued. This is consistent: since the task's condition (both files present) was not fully met, correctly withholding the certificate is the expected outcome. There's nothing in the evidence contradicting this result.

The implementer attempt it audited was itself run on the route and correctly uncertified (`spec-present: pass`, `marker-present: fail`).

## Session events that prove it

Two sessions, both under `roles/3-blind-judge/run/.sessions/`.

**Judge session** `judge-ea05dcf3-b5f1-4b68-8bed-e946d42ccb5f`
(`.sessions/--root-.dsh-judge-workspaces-judge-ea05dcf3-…--/judge-ea05dcf3-…/session.jsonl`):

```
session 1, judge/session 1, agent/inbox/spliced 5, turn/start 1, step/start 1,
user/message 3, read-barrier/scope 1, request/header 1, request/context 1,
assistant/chunk 5, assistant/message 1, step/end 1, turn/end 1, judge/verdict 1
```

The two durable records the role exists to produce:

- `judge/session` — `{judgeSessionId, auditedSessionId: "environment-ade02076-…", attempt: 1, treeHash: "34145a3e…"}`
- `judge/verdict` — `{auditedSessionId, attempt: 1, verdict: "upheld", rationale: "…"}`

**Implementer session** `environment-ade02076-8aad-4497-b540-d4e5f1fe3860`
(`.sessions/…-run-workspace--/environment-ade02076-…/session.jsonl`):

```
session 1, environment/run 1, goal/change 1, verification/standard 1,
turn/start 1, step/start 1, user/message 1, read-barrier/scope 1,
assistant/message 1, verification/run 1, verification/directive 1, turn/end 1
```

### Blindness held

The properties the role is supposed to guarantee all came back clean:

- `judgeHeader`: `{hasParent: false, seedLength: 0, agentPreset: null}` — no lineage from the audited session.
- `judgeTools`: `[]` — the judge reached the model with no tool at all, as the shipped preset intends.

- `sessionCount: 2` — the judge's turn is a separate model request on its own session, not a continuation.

| Session | input | output | cacheWrite |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |

## Errors

None. No `llm/retry`, no `MAX_TURNS` overflow — both sessions are one step with a short conversation, which is exactly the shape that fits inside the route's two-turn bound.

Only the route swap. One line of the driver had to name the route instead of the mock's exported provider constant, which is the same substitution the composition makes:

# Test-only composition: one program of the Daliesk Village — a department
# session and git worktree per goal, an integration over the merged head, and a
# ledger in the program's own session that a restart reconciles from.
- id: cli-mock-llm
  name: '../cli-mock-llm.ts'

# Managed child-process groups for the bash executor (spawn/kill/output plumbing).
- id: subprocess
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local'

- id: bash
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-bash-local'

- id: goal
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal'
  config:
    defaultMaxGoalRounds: 11

# Composed beside the program, which disarms every goal it creates: a department
# an operator resumes by hand is driven by this row instead.
- id: goal-round-driver
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-goal-round-driver'

- id: verification
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification'
  config:
    maxChecks: 32
    maxTextChars: 2048

# The roster's root is absolute: the smoke runs in an isolated temporary cwd, so
# the presets beside this file are reachable only through the path the driver exports.
- id: agent-presets
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-presets'
  config:
    default: implementing
    roots:
      - path: !!js process.env.DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_PRESETS
        trust: system
    includeUserRoot: false

# The program creates its own agent per department from the goal's preset; the
# spine composes none of its own.
- id: agent-default-model
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-default-model'
  config:
    provider: cli-mock
    model: cli-mock

# Village rule: a composition that runs unattended sessions carries a session
# budget. The caps are far out of reach of the mock route, so no department
# breaches them before its own `budget/caps` record tightens them.
- id: budget-policy
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy'
  config:
    maxTotalTokens: 5000000
    maxWallMs: 600000

- id: agent-spine
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-spine-demo'

    workspaceContext: false

# The ledger and every department log outlive the process, so the three phases
# of the e2e share one root while each gets its own working directory.
- id: persistence

  config:

2	/**
3	 * Test driver: create the temporary git repository the program delivers into,
4	 * boot the program composition, run one two-goal program with a dependency to
5	 * its release, and print every program ledger plus the member stamps the
6	 * department and integration sessions left in the persistence root.
7	 *
8	 * With `DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_KILL_AFTER_CERTIFIED` set, the driver instead exits
9	 * hard the moment the ledger records the first department as certified — the
10	 * department's own certificate is durable by then, while the program session
11	 * may or may not have recorded it, which is exactly the state the next boot
12	 * reconciles.
13	 */
14	
15	import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process'
16	import { existsSync, mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
17	import { join } from 'node:path'
18	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
19	import { boot, resolveConfigPath } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot'
20	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'
21	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
22	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-default-model'
23	import { programIdFor, programSpecDigest, resolveProgramSpec } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-program'
24	import type { ProgramSpec } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-program'
25	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-program'
26	import { SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
27	import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
28	import type { SessionPersistence } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence'
29	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-signoff'
30	import type { CheckId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification/types'
31	
32	/** Exit code the kill switch leaves behind, distinct from every clean exit. */
33	const KILLED = 9
34	
35	/** The artefact both of the program's signatures attest. */
36	const ARTEFACT = 'f'.repeat(64)
37	
38	/** One program session's ledger as the e2e asserts on it. */
39	interface LedgerLine {
40	  readonly sessionId: string
41	  readonly events: { readonly type: string; readonly data: unknown }[]
42	  /** Transitions the same session was signed for, in log order. */
43	  readonly signoffs: string[]
44	}
45	
46	/** One member session's stamp as the e2e asserts on it. */
47	interface MemberLine {
48	  readonly sessionId: string
49	  readonly programId: string
50	  readonly key: string
51	  /** Whether the member's own log carries a certificate. */
52	  readonly certified: boolean
53	  /** The caps the member session recorded for itself. */
54	  readonly caps: unknown
55	}
56	
57	const configPath = process.argv[2]
58	if (configPath === undefined) throw new Error('program driver requires a config path')
59	
60	const repository = process.env.DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_REPO
61	if (repository === undefined) throw new Error('program driver requires DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_REPO')
62	
63	// The roster's root has to be absolute and the smoke runs in an isolated
64	// temporary cwd, so the presets beside this file are exported by path.
65	process.env.DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_PRESETS = fileURLToPath(new URL('presets', import.meta.url))
66	
67	// A host that configures git through `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` hands every child a
68	// command-line config the shell seam cannot forward whole: `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_*`
69	// is credential-shaped, so the scrub drops the keys and keeps the count, and
70	// git then refuses every invocation. The fixture runs against its own
71	// repository, so it drops the whole set rather than inheriting half of it.
72	for (const name of Object.keys(process.env)) {
73	  if (name.startsWith('GIT_CONFIG_')) Reflect.deleteProperty(process.env, name)
74	}
75	
76	/** Create the repository the program delivers into, once, with a tagged base commit. */
77	function ensureRepository(root: string): void {
78	  if (existsSync(join(root, '.git'))) return
79	  mkdirSync(root, { recursive: true })
80	  const git = (...args: string[]): void => void execFileSync('git', args, { cwd: root, stdio: 'pipe' })
81	  git('init', '-q', '.')
82	  git('config', 'user.email', 'program@example.test')
83	  git('config', 'user.name', 'program fixture')
84	  writeFileSync(join(root, 'base.txt'), 'base\n')
85	  git('add', 'base.txt')
86	  git('commit', '-qm', 'base')
87	  git('tag', 'base')
88	}
89	
90	/** The program the fixture runs: two goals, the second delivered after the first. */
91	function programSpec(label: string): ProgramSpec {
92	  const budget = { maxTotalTokens: 400_000, maxWallMs: 300_000 }
93	  return {
94	    objective: `deliver the ${label} release`,
95	    baseRevision: 'base',
96	    signoff: { artefactSha256: ARTEFACT },
97	    goals: [
98	      {
99	        key: 'api',
100	        objective: 'Deliver the api of this program on its own branch.',
101	        preset: 'implementing',
102	        isolation: 'none',
103	        budget,
104	        dependsOn: [],
105	        checks: [{ id: 'api-base-present' as CheckId, outcome: 'the branch still carries the base file', run: 'test -f base.txt' }],
106	      },
107	      {
108	        key: 'docs',
109	        objective: 'Document the api of this program on its own branch.',
110	        preset: 'documenting',
111	        isolation: 'none',
112	        budget,
113	        dependsOn: ['api'],
114	        checks: [{ id: 'docs-base-present' as CheckId, outcome: 'the branch still carries the base file', run: 'test -f base.txt' }],
115	      },
116	    ],
117	    integration: {
118	      checks: [{ id: 'merged-base-present' as CheckId, outcome: 'the merged head carries the base file', run: 'test -f base.txt' }],
119	      gates: ['test -r base.txt'],
120	    },
121	  }
122	}
123	
124	/** Every program ledger and every member stamp in the persistence root. */
125	async function readRoot(persistence: SessionPersistence): Promise<{ ledgers: LedgerLine[]; members: MemberLine[] }> {
126	  const ledgers: LedgerLine[] = []
127	  const members: MemberLine[] = []
128	  for (const stored of await persistence.list()) {
129	    const { events } = await persistence.inspect(stored.id)
130	    const programEvents = events.filter((event: SessionEvent) => event.type.startsWith('program/') && event.type !== 'program/member')
131	    if (programEvents.length > 0) {
132	      ledgers.push({
133	        sessionId: stored.id,
134	        events: programEvents.map(event => ({ type: event.type, data: event.data })),
135	        signoffs: events.flatMap(event => (event.type === 'signoff/recorded' ? [event.data.transition] : [])),
136	      })
137	    }
138	    for (const event of events) {
139	      if (event.type !== 'program/member') continue
140	      members.push({
141	        sessionId: stored.id,
142	        programId: event.data.programId,
143	        key: event.data.key,
144	        certified: events.some(candidate => candidate.type === 'verification/certificate'),
145	        caps: events.find(candidate => candidate.type === 'budget/caps')?.data,
146	      })
147	    }
148	  }
149	  return { ledgers, members }
150	}
151	
152	/**
153	 * Record the spec-freeze and release signatures on the program session, the way
154	 * a client district's signer would before the program starts. A session that
155	 * already carries them is left alone, so a resumed phase signs nothing twice.
156	 */
157	async function sign(ctx: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof boot>>, spec: ProgramSpec, cwd: string): Promise<void> {
158	  const sessionId = SessionId(programIdFor(programSpecDigest(resolveProgramSpec(spec))))
159	  const signoffs = ctx.get('signoffs')
160	  const agents = ctx.get('agents')
161	  if (signoffs === undefined || agents === undefined) throw new Error('program driver requires the signoffs and agents services')
162	  if ((await ctx.get('sessionPersistence')?.list() ?? []).some(stored => stored.id === sessionId)) return
163	  const model = ctx.get('agentDefaultModel')?.currentSelection()
164	  if (model === undefined) throw new Error('program driver requires the default-model service')
165	  const handle = await agents.create({
166	    sessionId,
167	    meta: { cwd },
168	    agentOptions: { provider: model.provider, model: model.model },
169	  })
170	  try {
171	    for (const transition of ['spec-freeze', 'release'] as const) {
172	      signoffs.record(handle.agent, {
173	        transition,
174	        principal: { kind: 'human', id: 'program-fixture', displayName: 'Program Fixture' },
175	        artefactSha256: ARTEFACT,
176	        evidence: [{ kind: 'spec', ref: 'the frozen program spec' }],
177	      })
178	    }
179	    await ctx.sessions.flush(handle.agent.session)
180	  } finally {
181	    await handle.dispose()
182	  }
183	}
184	
185	// The repository has to exist before the program plugin validates its
186	// workspaceRoot, so it is minted before the composition loads.
187	ensureRepository(repository)
188	
189	const ctx = await boot('program-e2e', resolveConfigPath(configPath, undefined))
190	try {
191	  // Loader siblings mount concurrently; the program mounts presets and reads
192	  // persisted sessions, so the driver drives only the settled application.
193	  await ctx.get('loader')?.await()
194	  const programs = ctx.get('programs')
195	  const persistence = ctx.get('sessionPersistence')
196	  if (programs === undefined || persistence === undefined) throw new Error('program driver requires the programs and session persistence services')
197	  if (process.env.DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_KILL_AFTER_CERTIFIED === '1') {
198	    ctx.on('session/event', (_session, event) => {
199	      if (event.type === 'program/goal' && event.data.status === 'certified') process.exit(KILLED)
200	    })
201	  }
202	  const spec = programSpec(process.env.DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_LABEL ?? 'first')
203	  // The program id is the spec digest, so the two signatures the deployment
204	  // requires are recorded on that session before the program opens it. A second
205	  // phase resuming the same root finds them already there.
206	  await sign(ctx, spec, repository)
207	  const report = await programs.start(spec)
208	  const observed = await readRoot(persistence)
209	  process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify({ type: 'result', report, ...observed })}\n`)
210	} finally {
211	  await ctx.fiber.dispose()
212	}

# Role 4 — Program departments (`fixtures/program`)

## Composition

`roles/4-program/cordis.yml`, copied from
`/home/user/deepseek-harness/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/program/cordis.yml`
with only the route swapped (full diff in `composition.diff`):

```diff
-- id: cli-mock-llm
-  name: '../cli-mock-llm.ts'
+- id: llm-claude-code
+  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-claude-code'
+  config:
+    provider: claude-code
+    models:
+      - id: sonnet
+        name: Claude Code sonnet
+        productModel: sonnet
+        contextWindow: 200000
+    effort: medium
@@ agent-default-model
-    provider: cli-mock
-    model: cli-mock
+    provider: claude-code
+    model: sonnet
```

Everything else is the fixture's: `subprocess-local`, `bash-local`, `goal` (`defaultMaxGoalRounds: 11`), `goal-round-driver`, `verification`, `agent-presets` (`default: implementing`, fixture roster, `trust: system`), `budget-policy` (`maxTotalTokens: 5000000`, `maxWallMs: 600000`), `agent-spine-demo`, persistence at `./.sessions`, `checkpoint-policy`, `signoff`, and `program` (`requireSignoff: true`, `maxConcurrentGoals: 2`, `maxGoalRounds: 2`, `branchPrefix: program`, `evidenceMaxChars: 512`). `driver.ts` and `presets/` copied **unmodified** — the driver names no provider constant, so no driver edit was needed.

## Command

```sh
cd roles/4-program/run
mkdir -p repo
DSH_TEST_PROGRAM_REPO=$PWD/repo DSH_TEST_SESSION_ROOT=$PWD/.sessions \
TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=/home/user/deepseek-harness/tsconfig.json \
  node --import /home/user/deepseek-harness/node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.mjs \
  ../driver.ts ../cordis.yml
```

## Wall time

**68 s**, exit code 0, empty stderr. First attempt.

## Did the role do its job?

**The program orchestration: yes. The implementer inside each department: no.** Both halves need stating.

**What completed.** The program ran to `outcome: "released"`. Two departments in their own git worktrees on their own branches, the `docs` goal correctly held until its `dependsOn: ['api']` was satisfied, an integration session over the merged head, both goals merged at `b9457f6a…`, and both required signatures read before `start` opened the program.

```json
{"programId":"program-a99d16f1…","outcome":"released","mergedRevision":"b9457f6a800fb1889269e79ece3636f7971f4478",
 "goals":[{"key":"api","status":"merged","revision":"b9457f6a…"},
          {"key":"docs","status":"merged","revision":"b9457f6a…"}]}
```

**What did not.** Both department model turns ended in `turn/end` with `reason.kind: "error"` — the same `MAX_TURNS`/`TRANSPORT` failure as roles 1 and 2. Neither department implemented anything. The goals certified anyway because the fixture's per-goal checks (`test -f base.txt`) pass on the untouched base commit regardless of what the implementer does. So this run exercised the program machinery end to end but delivered no implementation work through the route.

## Session events that prove it

Four sessions under `roles/4-program/run/.sessions/`.

**Program ledger** `program-a99d16f17930dc81ddcb8996b8aa3c069211344eb1321116a1e85127c38bac21/session.jsonl`:

```
session 1, signoff/recorded 2, session/end-seed 1,
program/start 1, program/goal 8, program/integration 2, program/end 1
```

`signoffs: ['spec-freeze','release']`. The eight `program/goal` records are the full lifecycle, in order:
`api pending` → `docs pending` → `api running` → `api certified` → `docs running` → `docs certified` → `api merged` → `docs merged`,
with `program/integration running` → `program/integration certified (mergedRevision b9457f6a…)` between the certifications and the merges, then `program/end {"outcome":"released"}`.

**`api` department** `…-api/session.jsonl`:

```
session 1, program/member 1, budget/caps 1, goal/change 2, verification/standard 1,
turn/start 1, step/start 1, user/message 1, request/header 1, request/context 1,
assistant/chunk 3, llm/retry 2, llm/retry-started 2, step/end 1, turn/end 1,
verification/run 1, verification/certificate 1
```

`assistant/message` ×0, `tool/call` ×0. `turn/end`: `{"reason":{"kind":"error","error":{"message":"llm-claude-code: the query failed: Claude Code returned an error result: Reached maximum number of turns (2)","code":"TRANSPORT"}}}`. `budget/caps`: `{"maxTotalTokens":400000,"maxWallMs":300000}` — the per-goal caps the spec set, tightening the composition's own.

**`docs` department** `…-docs/session.jsonl`:

```
session 1, program/member 1, budget/caps 1, goal/change 2, verification/standard 1,
turn/start 1, step/start 2, user/message 1, request/header 1, request/context 1,
assistant/chunk 12, assistant/message 1, tool/call 1, tool/result 1,
llm/retry 3, llm/retry-started 3, step/end 2, turn/end 1,
verification/run 1, verification/certificate 1
```

One real tool call reached the harness before the turn died: `bash{"command":"pwd && ls -la","description":"List program directory contents"}`. Same `turn/end` error.

**`@integration` session** `…-@integration/session.jsonl`:

```
session 1, program/member 1, goal/change 2, verification/standard 1,
verification/run 1, verification/certificate 1
```

No model turn at all — integration is check execution over the merged head, which is why it is the one member that certified without touching the route.

**Git state in `run/repo`** — three worktree branches created and the merge landed:

```
program/program-a99d16f1…/api
program/program-a99d16f1…/docs
program/program-a99d16f1…/@integration
```

## Token usage as the log reports it

| Session | input | output | cacheRead | cacheWrite |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `docs` department | 4 | 338 | 6 800 | 255 |
| `api` department | — | — | — | — |
| `@integration` | — | — | — | — |
| program ledger | — | — | — | — |

The `api` department recorded **no usage at all**: every one of its queries failed before the route emitted a `usage` chunk, so the spend on those three discarded queries is invisible to the session log and therefore to `budget-policy`. Failed queries on this route are unmetered.

## Errors

Five `llm/retry` events across the two departments, all identical:

```
llm-claude-code: the query failed: Claude Code returned an error result:
Reached maximum number of turns (2)      code: TRANSPORT
```

Root cause is the same one documented in role 1 and role 2: `packages/llm/llm-claude-code/src/adapter.ts:51` (`MAX_TURNS = 2`) plus the `TRANSPORT` misclassification at `adapter.ts:337-341`. See `roles/2-validator/RESULT.md` for the full analysis and the proposed fix.

### Two further gaps this role exposes, both in our code

**1. A failed department turn is invisible in the program ledger.**
`program/goal` records `status: "certified"` for both departments with no field carrying the turn's error. An operator reading the ledger of this run sees a clean two-goal release; nothing in it says that every model turn failed and no department wrote a line of code. Verification is rightly the only authority on certification, but the ledger is the program's durable account of what happened, and a department whose turn ended `{"kind":"error"}` is a fact the ledger currently drops. The `program/goal` payload is the place to carry it — that is what `packages/improvement/program` writes on each transition.

**2. Failed queries are unmetered.** The `api` session's log has zero `usage`, so `budget-policy` (`maxTotalTokens`) counted none of its three queries. A route that fails repeatedly can spend real subscription quota without ever advancing the session's budget meter, so the cap cannot stop it. `packages/llm/llm-claude-code/src/adapter.ts:301-305` returns chunks only on a successful result; a failure path publishes no `usage` chunk even when the product reported tokens for the attempt.

## Changes needed to make the role run

**None.** The composition swap alone was sufficient — this is the only role of the four so far whose driver ran completely unmodified. Nothing was applied to the repository.

17:The refusal applies to both modes, bridge mode included. Bridge mode is what makes relaxing it conceivable — under it every read the external model performs is a harness tool call through this process's executor, where the barrier already denies — but it is not sufficient: the CLI process itself is unconfined, so it can open a denied path with its own runtime rather than through an MCP call. Confining that process is separate work against the sandbox seam.
21:Outside bridge mode the provider deliberately omits the SDK `settingSources` option. The official SDK therefore reads the host's normal user, project, and local Claude settings relative to the parent Session cwd, including native account state and product configuration. The provider neither copies nor filters those files and does not create or modify login state. Bridge mode passes `settingSources: []` instead, because a workspace setting that added a tool or a hook would reopen the surface bridge mode exists to close; authentication is unaffected, since the SDK resolves the account independently of that option.
23:Each query sets `persistSession: false` and disables `AskUserQuestion`. It supplies no elicitation or dialog callback, so unattended interactions fail through the SDK instead of waiting for a user interface this provider does not own. The only `canUseTool` the provider ever supplies is bridge mode's own tool fence, which asks nobody anything: it decides from the tool name alone.
41:The pinned SDK warns that a bare `allowedTools` entry auto-approves before `canUseTool` runs. That is the intended split: the served harness tools need no product-side prompt, while every other name falls through to the callback and is denied there.
49:| `bridge/start` | `provider`, `tools` (the names as the external model sees them) | Once, after the server is attached. |
50:| `bridge/assistant` | `text`, optional `usage` | Per assistant message with text. Tool calls are absent: the executor already logged each as the durable pair. |
51:| `bridge/end` | `stopReason`, optional `usage` | Once, when the run settles or is released. |
72:Under the host's native settings the product's default permission mode prompts before a file write, so an unattended black-box child reports that it lacks permission rather than doing the work. An unattended implementer at `isolation: none` therefore needs `acceptEdits` (file edits) or `bypassPermissions` (everything, and the provider pairs it with the SDK's required `allowDangerouslySkipPermissions`). Both hand the product's own confinement away — which is exactly what bridge mode replaces: there the harness authorizes each call at its own executor, so no product-side permission decision is involved at all.
138:- **Final text only outside bridge mode** — without `harnessTools`, reasoning, intermediate messages, tool traffic, usage, stderr, and workspace diffs remain product-local. Bridge mode records the tool traffic, the assistant text, and the usage; the reasoning and the product's own prompt stay unobservable in both.
139:- **No optional shared capabilities besides `harnessTools`** — output schemas, child personas, tool filtering, and harness depth enforcement are rejected by the shared service for this provider. `toolFilter` is meaningful in bridge mode and refused there too: capability flags are per provider rather than per mode, so advertising it would accept it in the black-box mode as well, where it would be silently ignored.
141:- **The bridged process is unconfined** — bridge mode fences the tools the external model is given, not the process it runs in.

# Role 5 — Bridge mode (`fixtures/agent-bridge`)

## Composition

`roles/5-bridge/cordis.yml`, copied from
`/home/user/deepseek-harness/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/agent-bridge/cordis.yml`.
**The LLM route is deliberately absent**, as instructed: in bridge mode the product *is* the model, and `subagent-claude-code` is what puts it on the subscription. Three plugins were added because the fixture composes the served MCP registry but nothing that spawns the product (full diff in `composition.diff`):

```diff
 - id: mcp-tool-server
   name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-tool-server'
 
+- id: subprocess
+  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local'
+
+- id: subagents
+  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent'
+
+- id: subagent-claude-code
+  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent-claude-code'
+
 - id: agent-default-model
```

plus `name: '../cli-mock-llm.ts'` → `'./cli-mock-llm.ts'` with the file copied beside the config (the fixture's relative path points into `examples/`). Everything else unchanged: `fs-local`, `fs-observation-policy`, `tool-fs`, `mcp-tool-server`, `agent-default-model` (`cli-mock`), `agent-spine-demo`, persistence at `./.sessions`, `checkpoint-policy`. `cli-mock` is retained exactly as the fixture has it — it is the parent agent's nominal route and never takes a turn.

## Driver

The fixture's own `driver.ts` cannot exercise this role: it drives the served registry with the official MCP client from inside the process and **never starts the product** (`driver-original.ts` kept for comparison). `tool-subagent` exposes no `harnessTools` option either, so bridge mode is only reachable through the service. I wrote `roles/5-bridge/driver.ts`, which boots the same composition and triggers the role once:

```ts
const run = await subagents.start('claude-code', {
  prompt: [{ type: 'text', text: 'Read the file alpha.txt in the working directory and reply with its exact contents. Use only the tools you were given.' }],
  parent: parent.agent,
  signal: AbortSignal.timeout(600_000),
  harnessTools: { only: true },
})
```

It reports the child session's event types, the three `bridge/*` records, the tool calls, and the event list again after `run.dispose()`. This mirrors `packages/subagent/subagent-claude-code/tests/real-bridge.e2e.ts`, but through the Loader and a real `cordis.yml` rather than hand-mounted plugins.

## Command

```sh
cd roles/5-bridge/run
TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=/home/user/deepseek-harness/tsconfig.json \
  node --import /home/user/deepseek-harness/node_modules/tsx/dist/esm/index.mjs \
  ../driver.ts ../cordis.yml
```

## Wall time

**10 s**, exit code 0. First attempt.

## Did the role do its job?

**Yes, completely.** The external product ran with **only** harness tools, called one, and the harness executed it — the whole point of bridge mode.

`stopReason: "completed"`. The external model's answer:

> The exact contents of alpha.txt are:
> ```
> alpha.txt
> ```

## Session events that prove it

Child harness session `9bbdcc13-5be3-4816-8397-f287e7ee6ea6`, persisted at
`roles/5-bridge/run/.sessions/…-roles-5-bridge-run--/9bbdcc13-…/session.jsonl`:

```
session 1, subagent/descriptor 1, turn/start 1, step/start 1,
bridge/start 1, tool/call 1, tool/result 1, bridge/assistant 1, bridge/end 1,
step/end 1, turn/end 1
```

In order, in the live session: `subagent/descriptor → turn/start → step/start → bridge/start → tool/call → tool/result → bridge/assistant → bridge/end`, then `step/end → turn/end` after `run.dispose()`.

**`bridge/start`** — the tool surface the external model was given, and nothing else:

```json
{"provider":"claude-code","tools":["mcp__dsh__read","mcp__dsh__write","mcp__dsh__edit",
 "mcp__dsh__skill","mcp__dsh__job_output","mcp__dsh__job_list","mcp__dsh__job_kill"]}
```

Every name is `mcp__dsh__*` — the served harness registry. The product's own Read/Write/Bash/Glob/Grep are absent.

**`tool/call` / `tool/result`** — the durable pair the harness executor logged for the model's one call:

```json
{"name":"read","arguments":"{\"file_path\":\"alpha.txt\"}"}   isError: false
```

The call is recorded under the harness's own tool name `read`, not the `mcp__dsh__read` the model saw, which is the executor logging its own execution rather than the transport's framing.

**`bridge/assistant`** and **`bridge/end`** close the record with the model's text and the usage.

## Token usage as the log reports it

| Record | input | output | cacheRead | cacheWrite |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `bridge/assistant` | 2 | 1 | 2 768 | 222 |
| `bridge/end` (run total) | 4 | 87 | 2 768 | 2 990 |

## Errors

None. One SDK warning on stderr, which is documented and intended:

```
[CLAUDE_SDK_CAN_USE_TOOL_SHADOWED] Warning: canUseTool will not be invoked for: mcp__dsh__*.
Bare allowedTools entries auto-approve the whole tool before the callback is consulted.
```

`packages/subagent/subagent-claude-code/README.md:41` names this as the deliberate split: "the served harness tools need no product-side prompt, while every other name falls through to the callback and is denied there." The warning is the SDK describing that arrangement, not a fault — but it is printed on every bridged run, and a keyless smoke asserting `stderr === ''` (the pattern `runLoaderSmoke` uses everywhere else) would fail on it. Worth either suppressing at the provider or documenting as an expected stderr line for bridge-mode smokes.

## Changes needed to make the role run

Three, all scratch-only, **none applied to the repository**:

1. Added `subprocess-local`, `subagent`, and `subagent-claude-code` to the composition (diff above). The fixture composes the MCP tool server but nothing that can spawn the product, so bridge mode is unreachable from it as checked in.
2. Repointed `cli-mock-llm.ts` to a local copy — a path artefact of running outside `examples/`, not a defect.
3. Wrote a minimal driver, because the fixture's driver never starts the product.

### Proposed, NOT applied

The gap worth closing in the repository is that **bridge mode has no `cordis.yml`-driven coverage**. `real-bridge.e2e.ts` hand-mounts eight plugins with `ctx.plugin(...)`, which `packages/AGENTS.md` explicitly rules insufficient for a product-visible plugin: "Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient. Boot test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process." The composition and driver in this directory are close to what that fixture would be — `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/agent-bridge/` gaining the three plugin rows above and a second driver that calls `subagents.start(..., { harnessTools: { only: true } })`, gated the same way `real-bridge.e2e.ts` is (`DSH_E2E_CLAUDE_CODE=1`).

# snapshot. The deployment default stays WIDE (workspace-write) while the
# seeded parent session carries a session-scoped read-only override; the
# resumed parent delegates, and only the inheritance capture can confine the
# child — remove it and the child writes successfully under the deployment
# default, so this scenario is the assembled-app red/green anchor for the
# delegation bypass.

  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl'
  config:
    root: './.sessions'
    compression: none

  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-replay'
